title: 2001: A Space Odyssey
hint_1: 1968. When astronauts weren't just floating in space but also pondering monoliths that might double as alien real estate agents.
hint_2: A supercomputer that could control a ship but not its own existential angst—turns out, even advanced AI didn't get therapy back in the '60s.
hint_3: You've seen this. Everyone's seen this. That you haven't guessed it yet may prove that monolith intelligence is still out of reach.
hint_4: Have an existential crisis while a giant baby stares into your soul. Neuralging over its meaning is optional but likely.

title: A Clockwork Orange
hint_1: 1971. The year when a film made ultra-violence look like a leading man had crash-landed in Beethoven's home, possibly against cultural zoning laws.
hint_2: Our lovable sociopath trades "A Little Help from My Friends" for conditioning so sinister, even Pavlov would cringe.
hint_3: Either you haven't seen this, or you have and that's somehow worse. Brace yourself for the world's most disturbing mixtape.
hint_4: Picture a milk bar, some eye clamps, and Beethoven’s symphonies getting more airplay than they deserved in this context.

title: A Nightmare on Elm Street
hint_1: 1984. There was nothing more comforting than a cozy bed. Except when your dreams were outsourcing their horror playlists to a striped sweater enthusiast.
hint_2: When the boogeyman wielded a knife-gloved hand and preyed on teen dreams, proof that REM cycles aren't always restful.
hint_3: At this point I have to ask — do you think sleep still sounds like a good idea? Because after this, I'm second-guessing my pillows.
hint_4: One, two, he's coming for you. Freddy's the kind of guy who turns bedtime into prime time for mortal dread. Sleep tight. Or don’t.
